2.title: Think like a programmer
2.description: Break a problem into steps. Explore sequences, decisions, and repetition.
objectives: Identify inputs, processing steps, and outputs.
Trace sequence, selection, repetition, and a simple search.
Write a short algorithm before coding.

3.title: Working with data
3.description: Give your programs something to work with: numbers, text, and user input.
objectives: Choose appropriate numeric, string, and Boolean types.
Convert keyboard input before performing arithmetic.
Format calculated results and explain string operations.

4.title: Making decisions
4.description: Use conditions to choose a path and check that input makes sense.
objectives: Write conditions with comparisons and Boolean operators.
Choose the correct branch, including boundary values.
Separate conversion errors from invalid ranges.

5.title: Learning to loop
5.description: Repeat useful work with for loops, while loops, accumulators, and menus.
objectives: Choose a for or while loop for a task.
Trace accumulators, counters, and sentinel values.
Keep menu state and ensure loops terminate.

6.title: Taking loops further
6.description: Practise nested loops, retries, break and continue, and tracing before the midterm.
objectives: Trace nested loops and reset inner counters correctly.
Diagnose off-by-one errors and retry invalid input.

1.title: Square Numbers – Iteration
1.description: Use input validation and loops to display square numbers within a range chosen by the user.
1.preparation: Review weeks 1–6, including the week 6 iteration material and pre-class activity, before starting.
1.submission: Submit your Python solution and documented plan to the assignment folder on DC Connect. Check DC Connect for the due date.
